Rashi on Yevamot 19b:10:1.hebrew: אי נימא אנולד לו אח - קודם מאמר, בהא לימא ר"ש "ביאת השניה כשרה"? והא דייקת מסיפא דבנולד ולבסוף ייבם לא פליג, והוה ליה אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, ודלמא מאמר קני וה"ל שניה צרת ערוה! ועוד, מאי "פוטרת צרתה" איכא? הא מיפטרה וקיימא, דאשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:10:1.english: If we say [that he refers] to [the case where] a brother was born to him - [i.e.,] prior to the levirate betrothal [ma'amar]: in this case, would Rabbi Shimon say, "The intercourse of the second [co-wife] is valid"? Why, you inferred from the latter clause that where [the brother] was born and ultimately he performed levirate marriage, [Rabbi Shimon] does not dispute — as she is the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist — and perhaps levirate betrothal acquires [her as a wife], so that the second [co-wife] becomes the co-wife of a forbidden relative [ervah]! And furthermore, what [meaning of] "she exempts her co-wife" is there [in this case]? Why, she is already exempt, for she is the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:10:2.hebrew: אלא אעשה בה מאמר ואח"כ נולד אח - ואשמועינן ברישא דמאמר ספק קונה לגמרי, ספק לא קונה, אפי' מקצת לא מהני, הלכך מייבם או חולץ לשניה ממ"נ: אי מאמר המת קנין גמור הוא, הוה ליה ייבם ולבסוף נולד, ואפילו קמייתא חזיא לייבומי; ואי לאו קנין גמור הוא, בתרייתא שריא, דלאו צרת ערוה היא, דקנין מקצת במאמר לית ליה לר"ש. ובסיפא אשמועינן דייבם ולבסוף נולד הוא דשריא, אבל נולד ולבסוף ייבם אסורה, דלא תימא "ביאתה או חליצתה" דקאמר ר"ש ברישא, אנולד ואח"כ עשה בה מאמר נמי קאי:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:10:2.english: Rather, [it refers] to [where] he performed levirate betrothal with her and afterward a brother was born - And [the Tanna] teaches us in the first clause that levirate betrothal [has a doubt:] perhaps it acquires completely, [and] perhaps it does not acquire [and] does not even take effect partially. Therefore, he performs levirate marriage or chalitzah with the second [wife] either way: if the levirate betrothal of the deceased [brother] is a complete acquisition, it is [a case where] he performed levirate marriage and afterward [the brother] was born, and even the first [wife] is fit for levirate marriage; and if it is not a complete acquisition, the second [wife] is permitted, for she is not the rival wife of a forbidden relative, since Rabbi Shimon does not hold of partial acquisition through levirate betrothal. And in the latter clause, [the Tanna] teaches us that it is [only where] he performed levirate marriage and afterward [the brother] was born that she is permitted, but [where the brother] was born and afterward he performed levirate marriage, she is forbidden — so that you should not say [that] "her intercourse or her chalitzah" that Rabbi Shimon stated in the first clause also refers to [where the brother] was born and afterward he performed levirate betrothal with her.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:11:1.hebrew: הויא צרה ודאי - זקוקה לייבם, דאי מאמר קני — תרווייהו חזו, דהוי ליה ייבם ולבסוף נולד; ואי מאמר לא קני — שניה חזיא, דלאו צרת ערוה היא. ובעלת מאמר, ספק זקוקה ספק אין זקוקה, דדלמא לא קני והוי אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, וחליצתה לאו חליצה לפטור את הודאית:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:11:1.english: The rival wife is definite - [She is] bound for levirate marriage, for if ma'amar [levirate betrothal] acquires [fully], both of them are fit [for the third brother], since it is [a case of] "[a brother] performed levirate marriage and [the other] was born afterward"; and if ma'amar does not acquire, the second [wife] is fit, for she is not the rival wife of a forbidden relative. Whereas the recipient of ma'amar is uncertainly bound [and] uncertainly not bound, for perhaps [ma'amar] does not acquire and she is [considered] the wife of his brother who did not coexist with him, and [thus] her chalitzah is not a [valid] chalitzah to exempt the definite [widow].

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:13:1.hebrew: מ"ט דרבנן - דאסרי בייבם ולבסוף נולד? הרי לא עמדה על זה בזיקת אחיו, שלא היה בעולמו מימיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:13:1.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis - who prohibit [her] in [a case where a brother] performed levirate marriage and afterward [another brother] was born? Behold, she did not stand before this [brother] with the levirate bond of his [first] brother, since he was never in his world [i.e., alive during his lifetime].

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:13:2.hebrew: ולקחה לו לאשה ויבמה - אע"ג שכנסה, עדיין קרויה יבמה. אית דגרס: אי הכי, תיבעי חליצה! אלמה תנן: כנסה, הרי היא כאשתו כו'. כלומר: אי הכי, דאשה שנתייבמה עדיין זיקה ראשונה עליה, תיבעי חליצה — כל אשה שנתייבמה ובא שני זה לגרשה, לא תסגי לה בגט:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:13:2.english: And take her to him to be his wife and consummate the levirate marriage [veyibbema] - Even though he has married her, she is still called a yevama. There are those who have the version [of the Gemara text]: "If so, let her require chalitzah! Why did we learn [in the Mishnah]: 'If he married her, she is like his wife, etc.'?" That is to say: if it is so that upon a woman who underwent levirate marriage the first levirate tie still rests, let her require chalitzah — [meaning that for] any woman who underwent levirate marriage and this second [brother] comes to divorce her, a bill of divorce [get] should not suffice for her.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:1.hebrew: ר"ש אומר ביאתה כו' - מפרש לקמיה דאעשה בה מאמר ואח"כ נולד לו אח קאי, ומשום דקסבר מאמר ספק קונה ספק אינו קונה, כדאמר לעיל, ומפרש ר"ש ואזיל:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:1.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Intercourse with her, etc. - [The Gemara] explains later that [this] refers to [the case where] he performed levirate betrothal with her and afterward a brother was born to him, and [it is] because he holds that [with] levirate betrothal it is uncertain whether it acquires [her] or does not acquire [her], as was stated above, and Rabbi Shimon proceeds to explain [this].

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:2.hebrew: חלץ לבעלת מאמר לא נפטרה צרה - כלומר: הא דקאמינא "ביאתה או חליצתה של אחת מהן פוטרת צרתה", כגון שיהא חולץ או מייבם לשניה, והראשונה פטורה ממ"נ. אי מאמר קני, הוי ליה ייבם ולבסוף נולד, ואפי' ראשונה מותרת לר' שמעון, ובחליצה דאידך מיפטרה, דהא מאמר ככנוסה והוו להו מבית אחד; ואי מאמר לא קני, הרי שפיר ייבם לשניה, דאשת אחיו שהיה בעולמו היא ואינ' צרת ערוה, וראשונה תצא משום אשת אחיו שלא הי' בעולמו. אבל חלץ לבעלת מאמר, שהיא ראשונה, לא נפטרה צרה; דדלמא מאמר לא קני, וממילא פטורה משום אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולם, וחליצתה אינה חליצה. והכי מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:2.english: If he performed ḥalitza with the one who received the levirate betrothal, the rival wife is not exempt - That is to say: that which I say, "intercourse or ḥalitza with one of them exempts her rival wife," [refers to a case] where he performs ḥalitza with or takes in levirate marriage the second [wife], and the first is exempt either way. If levirate betrothal [ma'amar] acquires [her as a wife], it is [a case of] one who took [her] in levirate marriage and afterward [the brother] was born, so even the first [wife] is permitted according to Rabbi Shimon, and through the ḥalitza of the other she is exempt, for levirate betrothal is like having taken her in [marriage] and they are both from one house. And if levirate betrothal does not acquire, then he rightly takes the second [wife] in levirate marriage, for she is the wife of his brother who was in his world [with whom he coexisted] and she is not the rival wife of a forbidden relative [ervah], while the first [wife] leaves [exempt] on account of [being] the wife of his brother who was not in his world. However, if he performed ḥalitza with the one who received the levirate betrothal, who is the first [wife], the rival wife is not exempt, because perhaps levirate betrothal does not acquire, and [the first wife] is automatically exempt on account of [being] the wife of his brother who was not in the world, so her ḥalitza is not [a valid] ḥalitza. And so [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:3.hebrew: או שנולד לו אח - דה"ל נולד ולבסוף ייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:3.english: Or if a brother was born to him - For it is [a case of a brother who was] born and afterward [the other brother] performed levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:4.hebrew: שתיהן פטורות - בהא לא פליג ר"ש, וכרב פפא:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:1:4.english: Both of them are exempt - In this [case], Rabbi Shimon does not disagree, and [this accords] with Rav Pappa.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:3:1.english: This section of the latter clause - [Referring to the case where] he performed levirate marriage and afterward [another brother] was born.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:3:2.hebrew: למאן קתני לה - כלומר, להודיע כחו של מי קתני לה בפני עצמה, ולא עירבה עם נולד ולבסוף ייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:3:2.english: According to whom is it taught - That is to say, to make known the force of whose [opinion] does [the Tanna] teach it by itself, and not combine it with [the case where] he was born and afterwards performed levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:3:3.hebrew: אילימא לר"מ - לאשמועינן דבהא נמי אסר, ולאו למימר דר"ש אהך לחודה הוא דפליג:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:3:3.english: If we say [it is taught] for Rabbi Meir - To teach us that in this [case] as well he forbids [her], and not to say that it is on this [case] alone that Rabbi Shimon disagrees.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:3:4.hebrew: לערבינהו - לבבי, וליתני ברישא הכי: כנסה ומת ואח"כ נולד לו אח, או שנולד לו אח ואח"כ כנסה ומת, או שכנסה ונולד לו אח ואח"כ מת — שתיהן פטורות. אלא מדפלגינהו ש"מ משום דאיירי בה ר"ש היא, דאשמועינן דבהא לחודה פליג משום דבא ומצאה בהיתר, אבל ברישא מודה:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:3:4.english: It should have combined them - [i.e.,] the clauses, and taught in the first clause as follows: "[If] he married her and died and afterward a brother was born to him, or [if] a brother was born to him and afterward he married her and died, or [if] he married her and a brother was born to him and afterward he died — both of them are exempt." Rather, from the fact that it separated them, learn from this [that it is] because Rabbi Shimon deals with it — it is [taught for] Rabbi Shimon — teaching us that in this [case] alone he disagrees, because he came and found her in a permitted state, whereas in the first clause he agrees.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:6:1.hebrew: אלא בעל כרחה - וקמ"ל דמאמר בע"כ ואפילו למקצת לא קני, ושניה יבומי נמי מייבמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:6:1.english: Rather, against her will - And [the baraita] teaches us that levirate betrothal (ma'amar) [performed] against her will does not acquire [her] even partially, and [therefore] the second [woman] may even be taken in levirate marriage (yibbum).

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:7:1.hebrew: ביאה דיבמה - אמרי' בפ"ק (דף ח:) "ויבמה" — בעל כרחה, דאם בא עליה אפי' באונס, קנאה:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:7:1.english: Intercourse with a yevama - We say in the first chapter (8b): "and he shall take her as a yevama" — [even] against her will, for if he has intercourse with her even by force, he acquires her.

Rashi on Yevamot 19b:7:2.hebrew: קדושין דעלמא - והלכה והיתה לאיש אחר (דברים כ״ד:ב׳), מדעתה משמע:
Rashi on Yevamot 19b:7:2.english: Betrothal in general - "And she goes and becomes another man's [wife]" (Deuteronomy 24:2) implies with her consent.

Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:1:1.hebrew: רבי שמעון אומר ביאתה או חליצתה כו' - פי' בקונטרס דקסבר ר' שמעון מאמר ספק קונה ספק אינו קונה, וכשייבם או חלץ לשניה נפטרת בעלת מאמר ממ"נ. ונראה שפי' כן דאין ר"ל שיקנה לר"ש מדרבנן, דא"כ לא היה יכול לייבם השניה, דהויא לה צרת אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו במאמר; אלא ודאי קסבר דקני לגמרי או לא קני כלל. וא"ת: אכתי צרתה היא בזיקה? וי"ל דר"ש סבר אין זיקה. ולר"י נראה דאפילו ס"ל דיש זיקה ומאמר קונה קצת מדרבנן — ניחא, דאין זיקה אוסרת ולא המאמר אלא היכא דאם היתה נשואה היתה אוסרת; וכאן אם היתה נשואה היא עצמה היתה מותרת לר"ש, דשרי ייבם ואח"כ נולד. ומ"מ אמת הוא דלר"ש אי לא קני מאמר — לא קני אפילו מדרבנן, מדקאמר לעיל: "אם מאמרו של שני אינו מאמר, אשת ראשון בועל", משמע דלא קני כלל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:1:1.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Intercourse or ḥalitzah with one of them, etc. - Rashi explained that Rabbi Shimon holds that ma'amar [levirate betrothal] is in doubt whether it acquires or does not acquire, and when he performs yibbum or ḥalitzah with the second [wife], the recipient of the ma'amar is exempt either way. And it appears that he explained it thus because one cannot say that it acquires according to Rabbi Shimon by rabbinic law, for if so, he would not be able to perform yibbum with the second [wife], since she would be the rival wife of the wife of his brother who was not in his world through ma'amar; rather, he certainly holds that it either acquires completely or does not acquire at all. And if you ask: She is still her rival wife through zikah [the levirate bond]? One can answer that Rabbi Shimon holds there is no zikah. And to Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] it appears that even if he holds there is zikah and ma'amar acquires slightly by rabbinic law, it is resolved, for neither zikah nor ma'amar prohibits [a rival wife] except where, had she been married [to the brother], she would have prohibited [her]; and here, if she had been married, she herself would have been permitted according to Rabbi Shimon, who permits [a case where] he performed yibbum and afterward [a brother] was born. Nevertheless, it is true that according to Rabbi Shimon, if ma'amar does not acquire, it does not acquire even by rabbinic law, from what [the Gemara] says above: "If the ma'amar of the second is not a valid ma'amar, he is having intercourse with the wife of the first," which implies that it does not acquire at all.

Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:1:2.hebrew: חלץ לבעלת מאמר לא נפטרה צרתה - וא"ת: ואמאי לא דייק מהכא תיובתא לר' אושעיא? דלדידיה, כיון דהוי זיקה ככנוסה, אמאי לא נפטרה הצרה? וי"ל: מדרבנן, כדאמר לעיל: גזירה משום שתי יבמות הבאות משני בתים — חדא מיחלצה, וחדא מיפטרה בלא כלום:
Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:1:2.english: [If] he performed ḥalitza with the one who received the levirate betrothal, her rival wife is not exempt - And if you ask: why does [the Gemara] not infer from here a refutation against Rabbi Oshaya? For according to him, since a levirate bond is [considered] like a married [woman], why is the rival wife not exempt? And one can answer: [It is] by rabbinic decree, as [the Gemara] said above — a decree on account of two yevamot coming from two houses, [where] one performs ḥalitza and one is exempted with nothing.

Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:1:3.hebrew: כנסה ומת ואח"כ נולד לו אח וכו' - הא מילתא דפשיטא היא, ולא הוה צריך כלל למתנייה, ואר"י דלא שנאה אלא לאשמועי' דהאי תנא עירובי מערב ותני מילי בהדי הדדי; ולהכי דייק מינה דבנולד ולבסוף ייבם לא פליג ר"ש, מדעריב ותני להו בהדי כנסה ומת ואח"כ נולד לו אח דמודה בה ר"ש, דאי בנולד ולבסוף ייבם פליג נמי ר"ש — א"כ בהדי סיפא הוה ליה למיערבה ולא בהדי רישא. והשתא א"ש דלא מותיב לר' אושעיא ממתני' דלא עריב ותני להו, דאברייתא שייך למידק כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:1:3.english: If he married her and died, and afterward a brother was born to him, etc. - This is an obvious matter, and there was no need at all to teach it [in the baraita]. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that [the Tanna] taught it only to inform us that this Tanna mixes and teaches matters together; and therefore [the Gemara] infers from it that in [the case of] "born first and afterward he performed levirate marriage," Rabbi Shimon does not disagree, since [the Tanna] mixes and teaches them together with "he married her and died, and afterward a brother was born to him," regarding which Rabbi Shimon concedes. For if Rabbi Shimon also disagreed regarding "born first and afterward he performed levirate marriage," then [the Tanna] should have mixed it with the latter clause and not with the former clause. And now it works out well that [the Gemara] does not raise an objection against Rabbi Oshaya from the Mishnah, which does not mix and teach them together, for it is on the baraita that this inference is applicable, as I explained.

Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:3:1.hebrew: לערבינהו ולתנינהו - לא כמו שפירש בקונטרס דאכולהו קאי, דאכנסה ומת ואח"כ נולד ודאי ל"פ ר"ש, אלא אתרי בתראי קאי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:3:1.english: It should have combined them and taught them - Not as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi] that [this] refers to all of them, for regarding [the case where] he married her and died and afterward [a brother] was born, Rabbi Shimon certainly does not disagree; rather, it refers to the latter two [cases].

Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:7:1.hebrew: גמרינן מביאה דיבמה - דאע"ג דמאמר אינו אלא מדרבנן, מ"מ מר מסתבר ליה דעשאוהו חכמים כביאה, ולמר מסתבר דעשאוהו כקדושין. וכה"ג איכא בפ"ק דב"מ (ד' יא. ושם), דקאמר: מר יליף מציאה מגט, אע"ג דלקטן לית ליה זכיה אלא מדרבנן, כדאמרי' בסוף הניזקין (גיטין סא. ושם):
Tosafot on Yevamot 19b:7:1.english: We learn from intercourse with a yevama - Even though ma'amar is only by rabbinic decree, nevertheless, to one [authority] it seems reasonable that the Sages treated it like intercourse, whereas to the other it seems reasonable that they treated it like [ordinary] betrothal. And similarly, there is [a case] in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (11a, and [see] there), where [the Gemara] says: One [authority] derives [the law of] a found object from [the law of] a bill of divorce, even though a minor has [the capacity for] acquisition only by rabbinic decree, as we say at the end of [chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 61a, and [see] there):
